Prescribed dose — metformin 500 mg twice daily, never titrated higher.

resolution.trap: A DPP-4 inhibitor is the right next drug for someone with no relevant comorbidity, but only after optimisation. Maximum tolerated dose means the highest dose he can take without adverse effects (usually 2 g).

clauses.text: A 49-year-old woman
clauses.feedback: Her age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed two years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: She takes standard-release metformin and empagliflozin.
clauses.feedback: Standard-release is the preparation NG28 offers to switch, not to abandon if adverse effects are encountered: modified-release metformin has not been tried.

clauses.text: She has had loose stools since her metformin dose was increased.
clauses.feedback: The timing points at the drug rather than a coincidence. It shows something must change.

clauses.text: She has no abdominal pain, blood in the stool or weight loss.
clauses.feedback: Nothing here points to an organic cause needing investigation, so the drug remains the explanation.

clauses.text: Her HbA1c is 51 mmol/mol and her eGFR is 91 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: An HbA1c near target and a normal eGFR rule out adding glycaemic control and withdrawing metformin for renal reasons. Tolerability is the problem left.

clauses.text: Metformin is to be stopped and a DPP-4 inhibitor started.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

resolution.lead: For someone already taking standard-release metformin, NG28 gives two options: continue it, or switch to modified-release metformin if the standard-release preparation is not tolerated or the person prefers it.
points: Standard-release metformin is the preparation she is on, so a switch is available.
People can experience fewer gastrointestinal adverse events with modified-release metformin.
Not tolerated is a conclusion to reach after the other preparation has been tried, not before.
resolution.trap: Switch to modified release formulation before considering stopping metformin

clauses.text: A 54-year-old woman
clauses.feedback: Her age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed six years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: She takes metformin, empagliflozin and semaglutide.
clauses.feedback: NG28 attaches a stopping rule at low weight to one of these three drugs.

clauses.text: She has lost 14 kg over the year since semaglutide was started and is pleased with the result.
clauses.feedback: Weight loss is what this drug is for, so a good result is no warning. The history cannot say if it crossed a threshold.

clauses.text: Her body mass index is 18.1 kg/m².
clauses.feedback: Below 18.5 kg/m² is underweight, and NG28 attaches an unconditional stop below that number for a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

clauses.text: Her HbA1c is 46 mmol/mol and her eGFR is 79 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: The HbA1c is at target and renal function is preserved, so neither forces a change. Good control does not override a stopping rule.

clauses.text: She is well controlled and is to be followed up in six months.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge. That she is controlled is a reason to change nothing about her glucose.

resolution.lead: NG28 says to stop a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide if the person becomes underweight, which it defines as a body mass index below 18.5 kg/m². Hers is 18.1, so the semaglutide stops.
points: Semaglutide is the only one of her three drugs the rule reaches; metformin and empagliflozin continue.
The instruction carries no conditions: benefit, satisfaction and glycaemic control do not prevent stopping it.
The weight loss is the reason to look at the number; the number is the reason to act.
resolution.trap: SGLT-2 inhibitor continues for cardiovascular or renal benefit, a GLP-1 receptor agonist stops only if it is not working and has no cardiovascular indication or the patient BMI is below 18.5 kg/m².

clauses.text: A 58-year-old man
clauses.feedback: His age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed five years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: He has no past medical history.
clauses.feedback: With no cardiovascular disease, nothing indicates the dulaglutide beyond glycaemic control. That is one of two conditions met — one left to check.

clauses.text: He takes metformin, dapagliflozin and dulaglutide for one year.
clauses.feedback: A year is long enough to judge the drug, but not a specific threshold to stop any of them.

clauses.text: His body mass index is 33 kg/m².
clauses.feedback: Obesity is why a GLP-1 receptor agonist was started. It does not prevent stopping a drug that is not working.

clauses.text: His HbA1c is 67 mmol/mol and his eGFR is 86 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: An HbA1c well above target means the dulaglutide has failed. That is the second condition met.

clauses.text: Dulaglutide is to be stopped and a DPP-4 inhibitor added.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

resolution.lead: NG28 says to stop a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide if it is not helping the person reach their glycaemic target and is not being taken for its cardiovascular benefits; for someone living with obesity, a DPP-4 inhibitor is offered next.

points.text: Not reaching target — a year on dulaglutide, HbA1c 67 mmol/mol.
No cardiovascular benefit to protect it — no past medical history.

resolution.trap: A sulfonylurea, pioglitazone or an insulin-based treatment come only if the DPP-4 inhibitor is contraindicated, not tolerated or not effective.

clauses.text: A 52-year-old man
clauses.feedback: His age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed five years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: He takes modified-release metformin, sitagliptin and dapagliflozin, all at the maximum tolerated dose.
clauses.feedback: Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor, and NG28 does not allow it alongside a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide. Same mechanism pathway

clauses.text: His body mass index is 34 kg/m² and he has no cardiovascular or renal disease.
clauses.feedback: A body mass index of 34 puts him in the obesity category, which makes him indicated for a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide.

clauses.text: His HbA1c is 69 mmol/mol and his eGFR is 82 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: An HbA1c of 69 mmol/mol shows further medicines are needed, which is a precondition for escalating. The eGFR raises no concern.

clauses.text: The plan is to start tirzepatide.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

resolution.lead: NG28 states the following: never a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide together with a DPP-4 inhibitor. Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor, so it should be stopped before tirzepatide starts.

points.text: At least 3 months on initial therapy. He is 5 years in.
Further medicine needed to reach his glycaemic target. His HbA1c is 69.
Not already taking one of these drugs.

resolution.trap: He is on a DPP-4 inhibitor, so a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide cannot start until it is stopped.

clauses.text: A 64-year-old woman
clauses.feedback: Her age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed four years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: She had a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction six weeks ago.
clauses.feedback: A myocardial infarction is atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and developing it after starting treatment adds subcutaneous semaglutide to the regimen.

clauses.text: She takes modified-release metformin and empagliflozin.
clauses.feedback: This is the pairing NG28 offers an adult with no relevant comorbidity, and it was correct when started. It is a base to add to.

clauses.text: Her blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg and she has never smoked.
clauses.feedback: Both are unremarkable, and neither changes what she is offered.

clauses.text: Her HbA1c is 42 mmol/mol and her eGFR is 76 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: An HbA1c of 42 is below target and the eGFR raises no concern, so nothing here argues for more glucose lowering.

clauses.text: Regular follow-up in three months is planned.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge. Booking a review does not establish that nothing is due before it.

resolution.lead: If an adult with type 2 diabetes develops atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease after starting initial treatment, NG28 offers to add subcutaneous semaglutide (Ozempic), up to 1 mg once a week, for its cardiovascular and renal benefits.
points: The addition is not glycaemic: her HbA1c is 42 mmol/mol, below target, and the drug is offered anyway.
Two triggers: an event, or a glycaemic shortfall. Here it is the event.
resolution.trap: If she presented with this history at diagnosis, all three drugs would have been offered from the start.

clauses.text: A 47-year-old man
clauses.feedback: His age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes six weeks ago.
clauses.feedback: 6 weeks is short of the 3 months NG28 asks for before this class of drug is considered.

clauses.text: He started modified-release metformin and then empagliflozin, and both are at the maximum tolerated dose.
clauses.feedback: Metformin first, then the SGLT-2 inhibitor at metformin's maximum tolerated dose, is the sequence NG28 asks for.

clauses.text: He has had no side effects and has not missed a dose.
clauses.feedback: Adverse effects and adherence are two things NG28 asks you to optimise before changing treatment; neither is present.

clauses.text: His body mass index is 36 kg/m².
clauses.feedback: Obesity is why this class of drug is being offered, but after meeting the criteria.

clauses.text: His HbA1c was 88 mmol/mol at diagnosis and is 71 mmol/mol today.
clauses.feedback: 71 is well above target and demands action, but it has fallen 17 points, which is what a regimen still working looks like.

clauses.text: Tirzepatide has been started.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

resolution.lead: NG28 considers a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide for obesity only if all three of these are present:

points.text: At least 3 months on initial therapy. He is 6 weeks in.
Further medicine needed to reach his glycaemic target. His HbA1c is 71.
Not already taking one of these drugs.

resolution.trap: The guideline does say to intensify medicines when HbA1c is not adequately controlled by the initial regimen and reaches 58 mmol/mol or higher, but this rule if the regimen has had its time.

clauses.text: A 56-year-old woman
clauses.feedback: Her age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: attends for review of type 2 diabetes diagnosed three years ago.
clauses.feedback: Diagnosis history, not relevant in this case.

clauses.text: She has taken modified-release metformin and dapagliflozin for two years.
clauses.feedback: Two years on treatment is well over the 3 months NG28 asks for. That is one of three conditions met — two left to check.

clauses.text: Her body mass index is 37 kg/m² and she has gained 4 kg over the past year.
clauses.feedback: Her weight is the strongest reason to want this drug. But NG28 only allows it here if her HbA1c is not controlled.

clauses.text: She has no cardiovascular or renal disease and her eGFR is 88 ml/min/1.73 m².
clauses.feedback: No cardiovascular disease and no renal impairment leaves her in the obesity pathway.

clauses.text: Her HbA1c is 46 mmol/mol.
clauses.feedback: 46 is below the 48 target for a regimen that does not cause hypoglycaemia. She does not need another drug.

clauses.text: The decision is to continue her current regimen.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

resolution.lead: NG28 only considers a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide for obesity if all three of these hold at once:

points.text: At least 3 months on initial therapy. She is two years in.
Further medicine needed to reach her glycaemic target. Her HbA1c is 46, and target is 48.
Not already taking one of these drugs.

resolution.trap: This is not a diabetes indication. The 4 kg gain is worth addressing, but not with this drug.

none.feedback: Continuing is a decision, and it is the right one.
